What is the area of the sector DOC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect OC, \\
$\because$ in $\triangle ODE$, $DO=4$, $OE=2$, \\
$\therefore \angle ODE=30^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $OD=OC$, \\
$\therefore \angle OCD=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle DOC=120^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of sector DOC $=\frac{120^\circ \cdot \pi \cdot 16}{360^\circ}=\boxed{\frac{16\pi}{3}}$.

Since C and B lie on the circle centered at O, equate distances: OC^2 = OB^2, so (2√3)^2 + h^2 = (h + 2)^2. Solve h = 2, hence R = 4. Now compute the central angle using vectors from O: vector OD = (-2√3, -2), vector OC = (2√3, -2). Their dot product is (-2√3)(2√3) + (-2)(-2) = -8, and each vector has length 4. C and D are the intersection points of chord CD and the circle, F is on the extension of CD, G is on the right-side arc, the extension line of AG passes through G to F, and BC has been connected. Since E is on DC, ∠ODE is the base angle at D of triangle DOC; also OD=OC, so ∠OCD=30°. Therefore the central angle ∠DOC=180°-30°-30°=120°. The area of sector DOC is (120/360)·π·4^2=16π/3.
